newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Toyota tight-lipped on European expansion.
newsitem.headline: Toyota tight-lipped on European expansion.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp said on Wednesday it was not satisfied with its European sales and would try to improve them.
But Japan's largest automobile manufacturer was tight-lipped on details of how it planned to achieve that goal.

"Considering that we hope to be a global player, the sales in Europe in 1996 were not satisfactory figures. We will take various measures to achieve the target of selling 600,000 cars in Europe in 2000," Toyota President Hiroshi Okuda said.
The company sold 420,000 cars in Europe in calendar 1996.
Toyota said in London on Wednesday it would invest 60 million stg ($98.1 million) in expanding operations at its British plant.
Focus has centred on where Toyota will choose among European nations to build its second plant after the one in Britain.
Some media reports have suggested that France and Poland are among sites in which Toyota is interested.
Okuda said the company would decide on the site of the new plant by the end of 1998.

"We have not decided in which country we will build a new plant in Europe. What we have decided so far is only that Toyota will start to produce new cars with smaller engines at the beginning of the next century," he told Japanese reporters here.
"Various countries invited us (to build a plant)," he added. We have done feasibility studies in five, six countries or something like that."
Okuda said they included France, Britain and eastern European countries.
Tatsuo Takahashi, president of Toyota Motor Europe Marketing & Engineering, said Poland was among the countries studied.
Okuda stirred up a row among Britain's Conservatives earlier this year by seeming to rule out building new factories in the country if it stayed out of Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU).
"I don't think EMU membership is the only factor. It's one among others such as the labour-management relationship, cost, productivity, and procurement of auto parts." Okuda said.
He declined to comment while the French election campaign was on progress on whether French membership of EMU would affect Toyota's decision on a new plant.
"I would not like to go far into political matters," he said.
VSZ a.s., Slovakia's largest steel maker said earlier this week it was in preliminary talks with an unspecified Japanese carmaker on building a car assembly plant in the country.
However, Okuda said that Toyota was not in talks with VSZ, adding that it was not among the countries on which Toyota has conducted feasibility studies.

Asked if Toyota could raise production in its plant in Turkey to boost sales in Europe, Okuda said that it would be possible, but that he did not think that the plant would be a base for Toyota's European operations.
